doc.title: James Moody interviewed by Monk Rowe, San Diego, California, February 13, 1998

title: Honors and feeling lucky
summary: He discusses the Hall of Fame and NEA Jazz Masters nominations and feeling lucky.

story.theme_name: Late-career reflections: awards, legacy and life lessons
story.community_name: Being honored: NEA Jazz Masters and other awards

blocks.x: Well you’ve got a growing list of recognitions here. The International Jazz Hall of Fame and Newark Hall of Fame, and the NEA Jazz Masters. So it’s nice to see that your career is being recognized.

Yeah it’s nice. I told my wife it was really nice — she came to me and she had tears in her eyes and she showed me this thing and it said that I was nominated. It’s nice to be nominated by your peers. I appreciate that. But I feel that I’m lucky, like very lucky, because I don’t say this in a derogatory way or a bad way, but like you take sperm? Like man I don’t know how many millions of sperm cells there are there. And like so even to be born we’re lucky. So for me to get that, I feel the same way, I was lucky.
